The requested change was to raise the AR Rendering service’s memory floor to 8 GB, set the recognition-only stage’s CPU floor to 5 cores, and tighten the end-to-end latency budgets for the Object Recognition Flow (≤ 455 ms) and the AR Rendering Flow (≤ 490 ms).

The current placement already meets the AR Rendering Flow latency (482 ms vs. 490 ms budget) and the AR Rendering service’s memory requirement (it is already on the edge node N4 with 10.2 GB used out of 9 GB, so the new 8 GB floor is already satisfied). However, the Object Recognition Flow currently runs at 473 ms, which exceeds its 455 ms budget, and the edge node N4 is already 1.17 GB over capacity.

A new configuration was therefore calculated. The Object Recognition service will be relocated from the edge node N4 to the cloud node N7. This move is necessary because keeping it on N4 would violate both the node’s RAM capacity (10.2 GB used vs. 9 GB available) and the Object Recognition Flow’s latency budget (473 ms vs. 455 ms). All other services remain in place. The new placement satisfies all updated requirements.

- the AR Rendering service now runs on the edge node N3, which has sufficient CPU head-room for the 9.5 vCPU requirement
- the Scene Processing service now runs on the cloud node N7, which has ample CPU capacity for the 12 vCPU requirement
- both the Object Recognition Flow and the AR Rendering Flow meet their 500 ms latency budgets in the new placement
